Information since June points to continued labor‑market strengthening and moderate growth, while both headline and core inflation remain below the 2% objective and market-based inflation compensation is low. In line with the expectations-augmented Phillips curve (Friedman; Phelps) and New Keynesian emphasis on expectations and interest-rate policy (Woodford; Christiano–Eichenbaum–Evans), the FOMC kept the federal funds rate at 1 to 1-1/4 percent and maintained reinvestments, favoring gradualism to preserve anchored inflation expectations. The focus on a symmetric 2% target and the plan to begin balance-sheet normalization “relatively soon” are consistent with Svensson’s inflation forecast targeting and a Rogoff-style conservative central bank approach to avoid the credibility losses seen in the 1970s Volcker-predecessor era. Overall tone is mildly positive on activity and employment, tempered by caution on sub-2% inflation and the need to monitor expectations.
